newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. calls special session on flood relief.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. calls special session on flood relief.

text.p: California Governor Pete Wilson on Tuesday called for a special session of the state Legislature to address recovery efforts in the wake of powerful winter storms that have caused severe flooding.

"I am calling on the Legislature to sit in extraordinary session to address the clear and immediate need of those individuals, businesses and farms victimized by those terrible floods," Wilson said in his State of the State address.
The special session will be convened on January 13. A special session waives certain rules, allowing the Legislature to act more quickly on relief measures.

Flooding in California has killed six people, damaged thousands of homes and inundated tens of thousands of acres of farmland. Wilson has declared a state of emergency in 42 California counties and the city of Morgan Hill.
Losses from California's New Year floods doubled to more than $1.5 billion on Tuesday and the floods looked set to become the most costly in the state's history, officials said.
